news.headline: Astronomers Spot a Brand-New Dwarf Planet
news.body: Astronomers think they have found a new dwarf planet beyond Pluto! It is nicknamed 2026 ED138 and sits about 4.3 billion miles from Earth. The Vera C. Rubin Observatory in Chile, which has the world's largest camera, snapped it over several months. If other scientists confirm it, it could become the sixth dwarf planet in our Solar System, joining Pluto, Ceres, Eris, Haumea, and Makemake.

news.headline: Beavers Help Keep the Land Wet and Green
news.body: New research from the University of Liverpool says beavers help landscapes even more than people thought. Their dams keep water levels steady, so peat and plants stay wet even in dry summers. At an enclosure in Cheshire, England, the beaver pond stayed wet through a big drought and helped nearby wildlife. Beavers once lived across Britain, and scientists say bringing them back can help wetlands.

news.headline: Penguin Poo Helps Green Snow Grow
news.body: Scientists in Colorado studied Antarctic snow and found something surprising: penguin poo, called guano, feeds tiny green snow algae. Where lots of penguins live, the algae grows faster and turns the snow green. Green snow soaks up more sunlight, so it melts a bit quicker than clean white snow. The researchers say this penguin effect should be counted when people study how Antarctic snow changes.

fun_fact: Dwarf planets are round like regular planets, but they share their neighborhood with other space rocks instead of clearing a path around the Sun! 🪐
